rag.body:
I study how AI can retrieve relevant documents to support its answers. I implemented aerospace document question answering using keyword, semantic, and relationship-based retrieval.


## Interest

smartfarm-rag.name: Evidence-based Document QA · SmartFarm RAG
smartfarm-rag.desc: Developed question-adaptive document retrieval for AI question answering, with a related KCI journal publication.
smartfarm-rag.body:
Developed question-adaptive document retrieval for AI question answering, with a related KCI journal publication.


## My role


Designed the research method, implemented the AI functionality, compared it with existing approaches, and wrote the first-author paper.


## What I built


Combined keyword, semantic, and relationship-based retrieval, selecting a suitable combination for each question. Connecting retrieved documents to AI-generated answers is known as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG).


Used prior comparisons of retrieval combinations to replace an additional AI call for choosing retrieval weights.


## Results and evaluation scope


Evidence: One related KCI journal publication


Compared retrieval methods on public data.


A separate SmartFarm operations system connects observations, document evidence, AI explanations, operator approval, and execution-result checks. This operational flow was validated in simulation.


## Technologies


Python · RAG · FastAPI. The research source repository is private.

rag-evaluation.title: RAG Evaluation Notes
rag-evaluation.summary: A practical evaluation lens for comparing RAG systems across retrieval quality, answer grounding, and operating cost.
rag-evaluation.body:
A practical evaluation lens for comparing RAG systems across retrieval quality, answer grounding, and operating cost.


## Why Evaluation Comes First


If you only look at answer quality in a RAG system, it is easy to miss the cause of failure. The retrieval, reranking, and generation stages need to be separated so you can see whether documents were missed, pushed down, or ignored during answer generation.


## Basic Metrics

- Recall@5: checks whether the supporting evidence appears in the top five retrieved documents.
- MRR: measures how early the first useful evidence appears.
- Groundedness: checks whether the answer is actually supported by retrieved documents.
